title: Signing with Herald and When I Meet My Girl
summary: Lee Allen produced for Al Silver; a demo ending with When I Meet My Girl led to a contract; Silver offered a Cadillac.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, Al Silver came down here.

And I had some tunes, and so I told Lee, I said, well look, I want to do a demo thing for him. He said, okay. So I made the demo tape. So I made the demo tape. I went to Cosmo studio, made the demo tape. No, how it happened was Lee Allen was doing the producing for Al Silver. And I had some tunes, and so I told Lee, I said, well, look, I want to do a demo thing for him. He said, okay. So I made the demo tape. I went to Cosmo Studio, made the demo tape. And then on the very end, I said, oh, I have this tune I had forgot about. And I called when I meet my girl. I said, I put it, the last tune I put on. And I didn't complete it. I put it on the tape. I sent it to New York. And Al Silver sent back a telegram. Said, record that last tune he did, When I Meet My Girl. And that was the tune on. Okay, that was the song for Al Silver. Then the next record was Baby Doodle Little, which was fair. Then the next seller I had with him, I've heard that story before. And so I had about five or six releases on Herald. And it was pretty good. Al was pretty nice. At least I got a few dollars on Al. You know, it's a funny thing. You know, you hear a lot of people like me, okay, because I didn't get this big number one record. I just didn't get paid. They just didn't pay me. Sign of the times. That's why I learned some sense on this record I got hit. It's a whole different ballgame. I got, now, if this record hit, my wife and them have some money if I'd have to die. If it would hit, I'd have a few dollars to think about. But, um.
What were you saying about Al Silver's, like, giving you the Cadillac?

Oh, he said, he told me one time, he said, he said, man, you make another record like when I meet my girl, and I buy you a Cadillac. And I said, well, don't buy me a Cadillac. Give me some money. And I still say, and even today, I don't necessarily like them big cars. I don't like a whole pile of jewelry. Boy, I'd buy a suit, and I'd rather have some money in my pocket. See, those are the two things. I like, I always say, well, I don't worry about clothes now like I used to. I'd buy a suit in a minute. But I don't do that no more. I need to buy some, because all my things are getting too small for me. But, uh. You're getting too small? Yeah.
Oh, yeah. I'm too small. Yeah. So I was about to spend a bit.
I'm about five. I'm, right now I'm about seven pounds out of a potion. And you see, I haven't eaten anything yet. That's the way it is. But.
